learnerStatement: Simulated learner. This review finds problems; it is not evidence that anyone learned.
learnerBoundary: Everyday numeracy, simple charts, comparison of numbers and familiar household objects; no domain-specific theory assumed.

observations.prediction: Selected about 67% against about 52% and about 33%, then locked it in.
observations.exploration: Clicked Roll 1, 2, 3, 4 sequentially. No-six counts were 1000 → 844 → 701 → 581 → 477; at least one six ended 523 (52%). Start over reset stage to zero rolls, 1000 no-six and 0 successes; revealed explanation remained describing the completed run.
observations.reveal: Show me why corrected prediction to about 52%; exact chance 1 − (5/6)^4 = 51.8%. Explained removing one sixth of remaining players rather than everyone; additive approach would exceed 100% on seventh roll.
observations.visual: Actual 1257 × 936 dark screenshot inspected. Descending gold bars with count labels, dashed comparison, sequential controls and final counters all visible.

prediction.reason: Plausible additive mistake contrasted with correct repeated-trial probability.

interaction.reason: Sequential rolls expose shrinking eligible group and working reset.
interaction.evidence: Counts 1000 to 477 over four steps; reset to 1000.

payoff.reason: Uses actual run counts to explain complement and additive failure boundary.
payoff.evidence: Reveal quotes 477/523, exact 51.8%, seventh-roll over-100% argument.

clarity.reason: Graph labels and gated next-roll controls clearly guide desktop path.

transfer.reason: Reusable count misses then subtract principle offered, but no new application with conditions.

accessibility.evidence: Keyboard, focus, contrast, phone, zoom and motion unknown.

surprise.reason: Committed additive prediction contradicted by final 52%.

visualExplanation.evidence: Five labeled bars in actual screenshot.

playfulness.evidence: Four sequential clicks and working Start over.

complexity.conceptualDemand: Requires following a changing denominator, then subtracting misses from total.

caveat: Only one completed run; reset clears the graph while retaining the prior run explanation, so its numbers no longer match current stage.
